entries.press: Open the Body combo and pick a body

args.name: body
args.meaning: Which body to explain

preconditions: Generation Ledger is open
entries.expected_output: Repoints both views at the chosen body and regenerates its per-pass record (one deterministic tile pass, then cached). Defaults to the canvas's active body. Cross-cutting selector - exempt from the toggle rule.
entries.reason_to_select: Chooses which body's generation to inspect.

entries.surface: History ledger, 'Body' combo (Story view only)
entries.press: Open the Body combo and pick a body

args.name: body
args.meaning: Which body's story to show

preconditions: History ledger is open
Active view is Story (Chain has no per-body selector)
entries.expected_output: Repoints the Story prose at the chosen body. Cross-cutting selector - exempt from the toggle rule.
entries.reason_to_select: Chooses which body's generation record to read - e.g. checking a prospective mining body's deposit story before committing.

entries.surface: History ledger, Chain view's round strip
entries.press: Click the 'System', 'Life', or 'Legacy' button

args.name: round
args.meaning: Which generation round to chart: System (physical), Life (biosphere), or Legacy (aftermath)

preconditions: History ledger is open
Chain view is active
entries.expected_output: Switches the Chain charts to that round's question (a caption states it). This strip is a plain selector - it does NOT close the ledger on re-click (no close flag is wired), unlike the top-level view tabs.
entries.reason_to_select: Each round answers a different comparison - which bodies are physically viable, which grew life, what remains - stepping through them builds the whole system picture.

entries.surface: History ledger, chevron on the tab row (Story view only)
entries.press: Click the fold chevron at the right end of the tab row
preconditions: History ledger is open
Active view is Story (Chain carries no view-level chevron; its stages carry their own)
entries.expected_output: Opens the Story view as a full-screen overlay, giving the biography prose the width the 380 px column breaks every line of. Re-clicking the chevron (or Esc) folds back to the in-column view.
entries.reason_to_select: A long body biography is unreadable as wrapped fragments in the column; expanding is how to read it as continuous prose.

entries.surface: History ledger, view tab strip
entries.press: Click the 'Story' or 'Chain' tab button

args.name: view
args.meaning: 'Story' (body biography prose) or 'Chain' (generation chain charts across all bodies)

preconditions: History ledger is open
entries.expected_output: Switches the view. Re-clicking the currently-active tab closes the whole History ledger (toggle rule); switching tabs is an ordinary view change. Story is about one body (see the Body selector); Chain compares every body side by side and hides the selector. A third tab, Tiles, was retired 2026-08-03 (BL-281) - it was a current-state readout in a ledger about the past; its buildings list is on the canvas and in the Selection element, its market data in the market surfaces.
entries.reason_to_select: Story answers 'what is this body's biography?'; Chain answers 'how do the bodies compare through the generation stages?' - the two halves of how this world came to be.

entries.surface: Balance Ledger (Budget), 'Laws' section beneath the two policy-tier stubs
entries.press: Click the checkbox beside a law's name to enact it, or click it again to repeal it (the standing toggle rule)

args.name: law_index
args.meaning: Which law on the books to flip. The prototype ships one: Extraction Levy.

preconditions: Balance Ledger is open
At least one law is on the books (seed_prototype_laws appends the Extraction Levy at world setup, un-enacted)
entries.expected_output: The law's enacted flag flips on the next mutable pass, and a toast names it ('Extraction Levy enacted.' / '... repealed.'). It takes effect from the NEXT economy tick, never retroactively on the quarter already accounted. While enacted, every unit of RAW output the corporation extracts is charged rate x units and the total appears on the Levies bar of the Corporations dashboard's Finance card. Prices do not move: a law is a modifier over the market, never an override of it, so the levy is a separate accounted cost rather than a worse sale price. Repeal restores the previous arithmetic exactly. Unlike ledger.budget_tax_tier and ledger.budget_wage_tier, this control is NOT a stub.
entries.reason_to_select: The only law lever that does anything today, and the one press that demonstrates the governing-body seam end to end. For a corporation SUBJECT to the levy it is pure cost, so a corp-side agent has no reason to enact it; it is here because the pivot's legislator needs the instrument to exist and to be observable before it can be negotiated (BL-280) or politicked over (BL-186, BL-345).

entries.surface: Market Ledger, 'Body' combo
entries.press: Open the Body combo and pick a body

args.name: body
args.meaning: Which body's markets to view; defaults to the home body

preconditions: Market Ledger is open
The body has at least one market
entries.expected_output: Repoints the ledger at the chosen body; the Market selector refills with that body's markets and the price/order tables refresh. A cross-cutting target selector - exempt from the toggle rule (re-picking the same body is a no-op, it never closes anything).
entries.reason_to_select: Prices differ per body; this chooses WHERE the price question is being asked - essential for comparing sale destinations.

entries.surface: Market Ledger, 'Market' combo
entries.press: Open the Market combo and pick a market centre on the selected body

args.name: market
args.meaning: Which market centre (city) on the selected body

preconditions: Market Ledger is open
Selected body has more than zero markets (auto-selects the first)
entries.expected_output: Repoints the price and sell-order tables at that market centre. Cross-cutting selector - exempt from the toggle rule.
entries.reason_to_select: A body can host several market centres with different books; this picks the exact venue for a trade.

entries.surface: Market Ledger, view tab strip at the top
entries.press: Click the 'Prices' or 'Sell Orders' tab button

args.name: view
args.meaning: 'Prices' (default) or 'Sell Orders'

preconditions: Market Ledger is open
entries.expected_output: Switches the ledger to that view. Re-clicking the CURRENTLY-ACTIVE tab closes the whole Market Ledger (toggle rule on tab strips); clicking the other tab is an ordinary view change. Prices shows the order book / price table for the selected market; Sell Orders shows the player's standing sell orders there.
entries.reason_to_select: Prices answers 'what is the market paying?'; Sell Orders answers 'what am I currently offering, at what floor?' - the two halves of a selling decision.

entries.surface: Nav rail, slot 2 (Budget icon)
entries.press: Click the ledger glyph on the left icon rail
preconditions: In-game
entries.expected_output: Toggles the Balance Ledger (Budget) open in the fold-out column; re-click closes it; opening closes any other open ledger. Open, it shows the money loop: income, costs, where the money went, a profit-per-tick line chart, a per-building profit rank table, and the stubbed Taxes/Wages tier controls. Single view - no sub-tabs.
entries.reason_to_select: Answers 'am I making or losing money, and which flow or building is responsible?' - feeds every spend/expand/cut decision.

entries.surface: Nav rail, slot 6 (Construction icon)
entries.press: Click the industry/factory glyph on the left icon rail
preconditions: In-game
entries.expected_output: Toggles the Construction panel open in the fold-out column; re-click closes; opening closes any other ledger. Open, it shows the Construction / Buildings split (defaults to Buildings): what is being built now, and the buildings the player owns with their management controls.
entries.reason_to_select: Answers 'what do I own and what is under way?' - the broad building overview; per-building operations (recipe, workforce, demolish) are reached from here but are separate presses.

entries.surface: Nav rail, slot 1 (Corporation overview icon)
entries.press: Click the corporation glyph on the left icon rail
preconditions: In-game (the rail is permanent chrome)
entries.expected_output: Toggles the Corporation dashboard open in the fold-out column. Opening it closes whichever other ledger was open (accordion). If it is already open, clicking again closes it (toggle rule). Open, it shows the player corporation's four roll-up cards - Production, Trade, Workforce, Finance - each a one-line verdict with an expand chevron.
entries.reason_to_select: Answers 'how is my corporation doing overall, and where is the weak card?' - the top-level health check that decides which subsystem to drill into next.

entries.surface: Nav rail, slot 8 (Diplomacy icon - provisionally hosts the corporations table)
entries.press: Click the diplomacy glyph on the left icon rail
preconditions: In-game
entries.expected_output: Toggles the all-corporations balance table open in the fold-out column; re-click closes; opening closes any other ledger. Open, it lists every corporation with its balance side by side (player row highlighted). Diplomacy itself is not built; this table is the slot's provisional occupant.
entries.reason_to_select: Answers 'how do rivals' finances compare to mine?' - the only side-by-side rival-balance read in the game.

entries.surface: Nav rail, slot 3 (Workforce icon - provisionally hosts the Economy panel)
entries.press: Click the workforce (population) glyph on the left icon rail
preconditions: In-game
entries.expected_output: Toggles the Economy panel open in the fold-out column; re-click closes; opening closes any other ledger. Open, it splits across three views - Corps (the player's balance trend, every corporation's balance, and the workforce table), Holdings (stockpile pools by body) and Markets (supply, demand and price per body). Workforce itself is not built; this panel is the slot's provisional occupant.
entries.reason_to_select: Answers 'what is the whole economy doing?' in one surface - balances, labour, stock on hand and market state side by side, rather than one body or one corporation at a time.

entries.surface: Nav rail, slot 9 (History icon)
entries.press: Click the history glyph on the left icon rail
preconditions: In-game
entries.expected_output: Toggles the History ledger open in the fold-out column; re-click closes; opening closes any other ledger. Open, it shows how the world was generated, split into Story and Chain views.
entries.reason_to_select: Answers 'why is this world the way it is?' - the body's biography and the generation chain behind it; feeds site-selection and understanding of deposit placement.

entries.surface: Nav rail, slot 5 (Market Ledger icon)
entries.press: Click the market glyph on the left icon rail
preconditions: In-game
entries.expected_output: Toggles the Market Ledger open in the fold-out column; re-click closes; opening closes any other ledger. Open, it shows prices, supply and demand for one market on one body (chosen by the Body and Market selectors), split into Prices and Sell Orders views.
entries.reason_to_select: Answers 'what does this good trade for, where?' - the price signal behind every sell-order, extraction and routing decision.

entries.surface: Selection band, body kind's action column, 'Go to surface' button
entries.press: Click 'Go to surface'
preconditions: A body (not the star) is selected
The body is surveyed (an unsurveyed body shows Dispatch Survey instead - a world-mutating press owned by the survey family)
entries.expected_output: Descends the canvas to the body's planetary tile surface (the most informative rung). Equivalent to the header's '>' for a body. No world change.
entries.reason_to_select: Surveying is done; the move now is to look at the ground - tiles, deposits, and rival footprints.

entries.surface: Selection band header (all kinds, including the tile card), 'x' button
entries.press: Click the 'x' button at the right of the band's header row
preconditions: Something is selected and the band is visible
entries.expected_output: Hides the band for this selection. It is not destroyed: the next selection (clicking any entity) reopens it. There is no other way to reopen it - the band has no nav-rail slot; selection is its only opener.
entries.reason_to_select: Clears the bottom band to see the canvas; costs nothing since any click re-summons it.

entries.surface: Selection band, tile card's right-hand 2x3 action grid, Construct (hammer) button
entries.press: Click the hammer icon button
preconditions: A tile is selected
Something is actually placeable on the tile (otherwise the button disables with 'Nothing can be built on this tile')
entries.expected_output: Opens the tile construction ledger (BL-162) in the fold-out column: every building type placeable on THIS tile, with full cost, expected-profit bar, and reason-coded validity. Opening it is non-mutating; the Build presses inside it belong to the construction action family. The button carries an accent ring ('primed') when the player has nothing under construction anywhere.
entries.reason_to_select: The front door to building on a specific tile - answers 'what could I put here and what would it earn?' before committing.

entries.surface: Selection band, resource drill view, '<' button at the left of its header
entries.press: Click the '<' (Back) button
preconditions: A resource drill is open (drill stack non-empty)
entries.expected_output: Pops one drill frame, returning to the previous view (usually the tile's metric accordion).
entries.reason_to_select: Done with the history; back to comparing the tile's other metrics.

entries.surface: Selection band, resource drill view, 'x' button at the right of its header
entries.press: Click the 'x' (Close) button
preconditions: A resource drill is open
entries.expected_output: Clears the entire drill stack AND hides the whole Selection band (unlike Back, which unwinds one level). The next selection reopens the band at its root.
entries.reason_to_select: Abandon the whole inspection in one press rather than backing out level by level.

entries.surface: Selection band, resource drill view, horizontal slider under the chart
entries.press: Drag the slider left (older) or right (most recent)

args.name: window_start
args.meaning: Left edge of the 8-quarter viewing window within the recorded history

preconditions: A resource drill is open
More history is recorded than the 8-quarter window (otherwise no slider draws)
entries.expected_output: Scrolls the 8-quarter window through the recorded series. Until dragged, the window tracks the most recent data as time advances; dragging pins it to the chosen position.
entries.reason_to_select: Reads earlier eras of the tile's output - was it always this productive, or is the deposit running down?

entries.surface: Selection band header, '>' (go-to) button
entries.press: Click the '>' button at the right of the band's header row
preconditions: Something is selected and the band is visible
Selection kind is not a tile (the tile layout carries no go-to; a tile's go-to is a no-op today)
entries.expected_output: Navigates to the selection - exactly equivalent to double-clicking it: a spatial entity (body, building, market, unit) moves the canvas (a body descends to its planetary surface); a non-spatial entity (nation, corporation) opens its ledger instead. The band itself stays; an open fold-out ledger is untouched.
entries.reason_to_select: The bridge from 'I am reading about it' to 'take me to where it lives' - the Host axis of the disclosure model.

entries.surface: Selection band, market/unit kind's action column, 'Go to' button
entries.press: Click 'Go to'
preconditions: A market or unit is selected
entries.expected_output: Navigates the canvas to the entity's position (its body's surface / location) via the same focus routing as the header '>' button. No world change.
entries.reason_to_select: Places the abstract row on the map - where IS this market or unit, and what surrounds it?

entries.surface: Selection band, tile card's action grid, Manage (gear) button
entries.press: Click the gear icon button
preconditions: A tile is selected
A building occupies the tile (otherwise disabled: 'No building here')
entries.expected_output: Switches the selection to the occupying building: next frame the band shows the building's own layout (profitability, its operating controls). Pure re-selection - nothing in the world changes.
entries.reason_to_select: The route from ground to operator: 'there is a building here - show me its numbers and controls.'

entries.surface: Selection band, tile card's metric chart (in-band or expanded)
entries.press: Click anywhere on a deposited-resource chart

args.name: resource
args.meaning: Implicit - the resource of the page currently shown

preconditions: A tile is selected
The current page is a deposited resource (Habitability/Hazard pages are NOT drillable - no per-tile history is tracked for them; their tooltip says so)
entries.expected_output: Drills into that resource's time-series history: the band (or overlay) replaces the comparison chart with the body's total as columns plus this tile's own series as a line, over a shared day axis. Hover tooltip announces 'Click for its history over time'. Pushes a frame onto the drill stack (max depth 20).
entries.reason_to_select: Moves from 'how good is this tile now?' to 'how has it produced over time?' - depletion and trend, the fact a long-term siting decision needs.

entries.surface: Selection band, tile card's metric accordion, fold chevron at the right of the pager row
entries.press: Click the chevron
preconditions: A tile is selected
entries.expected_output: Opens the current metric page as a full-screen overlay - the band rests expanded-in-place (its fixed rect cannot shrink), so the chevron means 'give this the whole screen', not 'fold'. Re-clicking (or Esc) closes the overlay back to the band. If a resource drill is open, the overlay shows the drilled time series instead.
entries.reason_to_select: The band's chart is 260 px tall; the overlay gives it the axis room and legend space to actually compare values.

entries.surface: Selection band, tile card's centre metric accordion, '<' / '>' arrow buttons
entries.press: Click the left or right arrow beside the metric title ('Name (i/N)')

args.name: direction
args.meaning: 'previous' or 'next' page

preconditions: A tile is selected
Not already at the first/last page (the arrow disables at the ends)
entries.expected_output: Pages the accordion to the adjacent metric: one page per resource deposited on the tile (this tile's yield vs a top-10% tile), then the tile's Habitability and Hazard scalars (vs the body average). One titled chart shows at a time.
entries.reason_to_select: Walks every measurable fact about the tile one chart at a time - the read that grades a prospective build site.

entries.surface: Keyboard, in-game only
entries.press: Press Esc.
preconditions: App is in game. On the main menu and the wizard, Esc does nothing (the key handler returns before Esc handling on those screens).
Works even while an ImGui panel holds keyboard focus — Esc is handled before the ImGui keyboard guard.
entries.expected_output: Exactly one rung of this precedence ladder fires, highest first: (1) an armed exit-confirm backs out (Really quit? disarms); (2) an open system menu closes; (3) if the sticky selection card is open and has a drill stack, one drill level unwinds; (4) if the corporation roll-up is drilled into a constituent, it returns to the roll-up; (5) if a fold overlay is expanded full-screen, it folds up; (6) an open sticky card hides (hidden for this selection, not destroyed); (7) otherwise the system menu opens. One press never does two of these — e.g. Esc reaches the menu only once the card is fully closed.
entries.reason_to_select: The universal step-out key: back out of a confirmation, close the menu, unwind a drill, fold an overlay, dismiss the card — or, with nothing open, reach the session menu.

entries.surface: Keyboard; opens the centred Options window
entries.press: Press F10 (press again, click Close, or click the window's X to dismiss).
preconditions: App is in game.
Not while an ImGui widget owns the keyboard.
entries.expected_output: Toggles the Options window: a Display section (Resolution preset combo, Fullscreen, VSync), an Accessibility section (UI Scale), a live window-size readout, and Close. Every change applies live to the SDL window and persists to options.cfg immediately.
entries.reason_to_select: To adjust display and UI-scale settings mid-session.

entries.surface: Keyboard; works on every screen (menu, wizard, and in game)
entries.press: Press F11 (press again, or use the HUD's own close button, to put it away).
preconditions: None — handled before the screen guard, so the frame budget can be watched on the menu and the generation screen too.
entries.expected_output: Toggles the frame-budget HUD, the per-frame timing instrument. In game it first anchors top-left of the canvas area (movable after); on the pre-play screens it insets from the top-left corner. Honest status: this is a dev/audit instrument (the v0.1.0 performance audit tool), not shipped player chrome, and it sits outside the shared canvas command vocabulary.
entries.reason_to_select: To watch build/submit/present frame costs while reproducing a performance concern.

entries.surface: Keyboard; works on every screen and regardless of focus
entries.press: Press F12.
preconditions: None — handled first in the key handler, before the screen guard and the ImGui keyboard guard.
entries.expected_output: The exact composited frame (captured before present) is written as a PNG to screenshots/io_<ticks>.png in the working directory, creating the screenshots/ folder if needed. In interactive play there is no golden comparison — named captures and golden diffing belong to the --verify harness, not F12.
entries.reason_to_select: To record what is on screen — evidence for a bug report, a layout question, or a state worth keeping.

entries.surface: Keyboard; opens a centred Key Bindings window
entries.press: Press F1 (press again, or click the window's X, to close).
preconditions: App is in game (the binding table is gated off on the menu and wizard).
Not while an ImGui widget owns the keyboard (typing in a text field suppresses it).
entries.expected_output: Toggles a two-column Action/Key cheat-sheet, generated from the same binding table the key handler loops over, so it can never drift from the real bindings. F11 and F12 sit outside that table and are appended to the sheet by hand.
entries.reason_to_select: To look up every keyboard shortcut without leaving the game.

entries.surface: Keyboard; opens the mock tech-tree viewer
entries.press: Press F9 (press again to close).
preconditions: App is in game.
Not while an ImGui widget owns the keyboard.
entries.expected_output: Toggles a read-only viewer over scripts/tech_tree.lua, tabbed by era: Era -1 Antiquity (placeholder pointing at the BL-307 ladder store), Era 0, Era 1, and Standing lines; eras with no authored quests show a placeholder. Honest status: this is a mock — a design aid with no simulation coupling; nothing can be researched and nothing in the world reads it.
entries.reason_to_select: To browse the drafted tech-tree content; of no strategic use to an AI player yet.

entries.surface: In-game chrome, top-right gear button just left of the time column
entries.press: Click the gear (three-bar) button.
preconditions: App is in game (app_screen::in_game).
entries.expected_output: Toggles the small system-menu popup open or closed beneath the gear. Closing it via the gear also disarms any pending exit confirmation.
entries.reason_to_select: Mouse route to the session controls (Pause/Resume, Exit Game); Esc is the keyboard parity for the same popup.

entries.surface: Main menu, New World block, Copy seed button
entries.press: Click Copy seed.
preconditions: App is on the main menu screen.
entries.expected_output: The current seed, formatted as 8 hex digits, is placed on the system clipboard. Nothing else changes.
entries.reason_to_select: To record or share the reproducible key for the world about to be generated.

entries.surface: Main menu, primary button column
entries.press: Click New Game.
preconditions: App is on the main menu screen.
entries.expected_output: The screen transitions to the New World wizard (app_screen::generating), opening on round 1 of 3. Nothing is generated or committed by this press; the wizard only previews.
entries.reason_to_select: To start setting up a new world; this is the only route into play.

entries.surface: Main menu, primary button column
entries.press: Click Quit.
preconditions: App is on the main menu screen.
entries.expected_output: The application requests quit and exits. No confirmation is asked here (nothing exists to lose on the menu). Settings were already persisted to options.cfg as they changed.
entries.reason_to_select: To leave the application from the entry screen.

entries.surface: Main menu, New World block, Roll button beside the seed field
entries.press: Click Roll.
preconditions: App is on the main menu screen.
entries.expected_output: The seed field is replaced with a fresh random draw (a one-shot random_device read; the only place entropy touches the pipeline). No world is generated yet.
entries.reason_to_select: To get a fresh world without caring which one; the seed shown remains the reproducible key.

entries.surface: Main menu, New World block, Resources radio row
entries.press: Click one of the three radio buttons: Sparse, Lean, or Standard.

args.name: level
args.meaning: Resource abundance tier. Standard is the Earth-like ceiling; Sparse and Lean step down from it. There is no tier above Standard.

preconditions: App is on the main menu screen.
entries.expected_output: The pending world parameters carry the chosen abundance level, consumed at Begin. The Bodies slider next to this row is disabled (fixed at 5) and cannot be pressed.
entries.reason_to_select: To choose how resource-rich the generated world is; leaner tiers make extraction siting and trade tighter.

entries.surface: Main menu, New World block, Seed field
entries.press: Type an 8-digit hex value into the seed input box.

args.name: seed
args.meaning: The world seed. Generation is a pure function of this value plus the knobs: same seed and knobs give an identical world.

preconditions: App is on the main menu screen (app_screen::menu).
entries.expected_output: The pending world parameters carry the typed seed. Nothing is generated; the seed is consumed only when the wizard's Begin is pressed.
entries.reason_to_select: To reproduce a specific known world, or to share/compare a world by its seed.

entries.surface: Options window, bottom
entries.press: Click Close.
preconditions: Options window open.
entries.expected_output: The Options window closes. All changes were already applied and saved as they were made; Close commits nothing.
entries.reason_to_select: To put the window away after adjusting settings.

entries.surface: Options window, Display section
entries.press: Click the Fullscreen checkbox.

args.name: on
args.meaning: Target state; the press toggles the current one.

preconditions: Options window open.
entries.expected_output: Fullscreen applies live and persists to options.cfg immediately. While on, the Resolution combo is disabled; the stored windowed size is set first so leaving fullscreen restores it.
entries.reason_to_select: To switch between fullscreen and windowed play.

entries.surface: Options window, Display section, Resolution combo
entries.press: Open the combo and click a preset.

args.name: preset
args.meaning: Windowed size preset. A free drag-resize of the frame shows as 'Custom' in the combo.

preconditions: Options window open; Fullscreen is off (the combo is disabled while fullscreen).
entries.expected_output: The SDL window resizes immediately and the choice persists to options.cfg at once.
entries.reason_to_select: To fit the window to the display or to a capture-friendly size.

entries.surface: Options window, Accessibility section, UI Scale combo
entries.press: Open the combo and click a step.

args.name: step
args.meaning: Global UI scale step (stored as index 0-2; a corrupt config clamps back into this range).

preconditions: Options window open.
entries.expected_output: UI scale applies live and persists to options.cfg immediately.
entries.reason_to_select: To make the interface legible on dense or high-DPI displays.

entries.surface: Options window, Display section
entries.press: Click the VSync checkbox.

args.name: on
args.meaning: Target state; the press toggles the current one.

preconditions: Options window open.
entries.expected_output: Vertical sync applies live to the renderer and persists to options.cfg immediately.
entries.reason_to_select: To trade tearing against frame latency, or to uncap frames when measuring with the F11 HUD.

entries.surface: System menu popup, below the separator
entries.press: Click Exit Game.
preconditions: App is in game; the system menu popup is open; no exit confirmation is currently armed.
entries.expected_output: Arms an inline confirmation: the button is replaced by a 'Really quit?' prompt with Yes, quit and Cancel. Nothing exits yet. The confirm exists because there is no save in the prototype — quitting discards the session.
entries.reason_to_select: First step of leaving a session deliberately, with a guard against a stray click.

entries.surface: System menu popup, armed exit confirmation
entries.press: Click Cancel (or press Esc, which backs the armed confirm out as its highest-precedence rung).
preconditions: App is in game; the exit confirmation is armed.
entries.expected_output: The confirmation disarms and the popup returns to showing Exit Game. Play continues unaffected.
entries.reason_to_select: To back out of an exit started by mistake.

entries.surface: System menu popup, armed exit confirmation
entries.press: Click Yes, quit.
preconditions: App is in game; the system menu is open and the exit confirmation is armed.
entries.expected_output: The application quits. The session is not saved (there is no save in the prototype); display settings already live in options.cfg.
entries.reason_to_select: To end the session for good.

entries.surface: System menu popup, top button
entries.press: Click Pause (or Resume — the label reflects the current sim state).
preconditions: App is in game; the system menu popup is open.
entries.expected_output: Toggles simulation pause via the same pause_toggle path as the Space hotkey. Resuming restores the previous speed tier. The button label flips accordingly.
entries.reason_to_select: To halt or resume the simulation clock from the mouse-driven session menu.

entries.surface: Tech-tree viewer (F9), era tab strip
entries.press: Click the 'Era -1 Antiquity', 'Era 0 — Terrestrial', 'Era 1 — Early Space' or 'Standing lines' tab button

args.name: view
args.meaning: 'Era -1 Antiquity' (placeholder pointing at the BL-307 ladder store) / 'Era 0 — Terrestrial' (the default) / 'Era 1 — Early Space' / 'Standing lines' (span eras, never gate one)

preconditions: Tech-tree viewer is open (F9)
entries.expected_output: Switches which era's tree is shown — each era carries its own tree; eras with no authored quests show a placeholder. Re-clicking the currently-active tab closes the viewer (toggle rule); switching tabs is an ordinary view change.
entries.reason_to_select: To browse a specific era's drafted content; of no strategic use to an AI player yet — the viewer is a mock with no simulation coupling.

entries.surface: New World wizard, footer button row
entries.press: Click Back.
preconditions: App is on the wizard screen.
entries.expected_output: On rounds 2-3: steps back one round (a plain revision — there is no per-round snapshot, since rounds are causal). On round 1: returns to the main menu. Leaving costs nothing (nothing is generated until Begin), and preferences survive the trip, so re-entering resumes the same leans from round 1.
entries.reason_to_select: To revise an earlier round's preferences, or to abandon world setup and return to the menu.

entries.surface: New World wizard, footer button row (right edge), final round
entries.press: Click Begin.
preconditions: App is on the wizard screen, on the last round (round 3 of 3).
entries.expected_output: The one and only generation call (start_new_game): the sim clock is rebased, the world is built from the pending parameters, the economy loads, a pre-game warm start runs 12 quarterly ticks (~3 in-game years) so play opens onto live markets and non-empty pools, the clock is rebased again, and the screen transitions to in_game. Play opens on the corporation's home planet at the Planetary rung with the home body selected.
entries.reason_to_select: To commit the chosen seed and preferences and start the campaign.

entries.surface: New World wizard, footer button row (right edge)
entries.press: Click Continue.
preconditions: App is on the wizard screen, on round 1 or 2 (any round except the last).
entries.expected_output: Advances to the next round. The button reads Continue on non-final rounds and Begin on the last; this press generates nothing.
entries.reason_to_select: To accept this round's roll and preferences and move to the next batch of decisions.

entries.surface: New World wizard, footer button row
entries.press: Click Reroll.
preconditions: App is on the wizard screen.
entries.expected_output: The current round is re-drawn from a fresh number under the same preferences, and — because the chain is causal — everything downstream of it re-draws too. Charts refresh; nothing is generated. Rounds already behind the player are not re-rolled by this press.
entries.reason_to_select: To get a different concrete roll for this round's stages without changing any stated preference.

entries.surface: New World wizard, the preference block at the bottom of the current round
entries.press: Click one of the four segmented options on a preference row: Any, or the row's low/mid/high named lean.

args.name: axis
args.meaning: Round 1 rows: Star (Dimmer / Sun-like / Brighter), World (Small / Earth-like / Large), Interior (Old and cold / Moderate / Young and vigorous), Metal (Metal-poor / Normal / Metal-rich). Round 2 rows: Ocean (Continental / Balanced / Oceanic), Oxygen (Oxygenated early / Balanced / Oxygenated late), Coal basins (Seasonal / Mixed / Everwet). Round 3 row: Drawdown (Barely touched / Worked / Stripped).

args.name: lean
args.meaning: A named lean, not a parameter: it narrows the range the seed is sampled from and never pins a value. No raw generated number is editable or shown in the decision area.

preconditions: App is on the wizard screen, on the round that owns the row.
entries.expected_output: The preview chain re-runs as a pure throwaway (resolve_preferences + preview_system); the charts above update to show the new roll. The world itself (m_world) is untouched. Resolution internally rerolls until the homeworld clears the Earth-like floor; if it took more than one draw the screen says 'Found on attempt N', and if no draw cleared the floor it says so and shows the closest world found. The Oxygen row carries the one spelled-out trade: oxygenated early is coal-rich and iron-lean, oxygenated late is iron-rich and coal-lean.
entries.reason_to_select: To bias the generated world along a named axis — resource character, land/ocean split, remaining untapped deposits — while keeping generation seed-driven.

entries.surface: New World wizard, the charts area of the current round
entries.press: Click a stage's fold row (its one-line verdict) to expand it; click again to fold it back to the verdict line.

args.name: stage
args.type: chain stage within the current round
args.meaning: Which of the round's Planetology stages to open. Round 1 covers the star/world/interior/metal stages, round 2 the ocean/oxygen/coal stages, round 3 the drawdown stage.

preconditions: App is on the wizard screen (app_screen::generating).
entries.expected_output: The stage expands from its verdict line into its full chart-and-explanation view, or folds back. Purely presentational; no preference or preview state changes. This is the same fold idiom the in-game ledgers use — the wizard is where it is taught.
entries.reason_to_select: To inspect what the current roll actually produced for a stage before setting or judging a preference; the charts are the only honest feedback (no raw values are printed).

entries.surface: Navigation rail slot 11, "AI decisions"
entries.press: Click nav rail slot 11 to open the AI decision feed; click it again to close
preconditions: In game (not the menu or the generation screen)
entries.expected_output: The AI decision feed opens in the shell fold-out column, closing whatever ledger was open (the column holds one occupant). It lists recent strategic decisions newest-first: date, corporation, verb and target, reason, and the winning/runner-up score pair. Clicking the slot while the feed is already open closes it (standing toggle rule).
entries.reason_to_select: To read WHY the rival corporations did what they did, and how close each call was - the only surface that exposes the scorer's rationale. A near-tied margin means the tuning could have gone the other way; a wide one means conviction.

entries.surface: AI decision feed, corporation filter
entries.press: Select a corporation from the feed's corp selector, or "All"

args.name: corp
args.meaning: Which corporation's decisions to show; "all" clears the filter

preconditions: AI decision feed is open
entries.expected_output: The list narrows to that corporation's decisions. The filter persists across selection changes elsewhere in the game - clicking a tile does not clear it.
entries.reason_to_select: To follow ONE competitor's run rather than the whole field. Reading a single corp's decisions in order is how a strategy becomes visible as a sequence rather than as noise.

entries.surface: AI decision feed, reason filter
entries.press: Select a decision reason from the feed's reason selector, or "All"

args.name: reason
args.meaning: best_build / dial_workforce / dial_recipe / dial_idle / dial_resume / survey_expand / hire_available / trade_surplus

preconditions: AI decision feed is open
entries.expected_output: The list narrows to decisions taken for that reason, across every corporation unless the corp filter is also set.
entries.reason_to_select: To ask a specific question of the run rather than scroll it. 'Every solvency-defence idle' and 'every build' are different questions, and the reason code is what separates them.

entries.surface: Corporation panel, Stance column. Confirm popup on press (demolish precedent — not literally irreversible, but not unilaterally reversible by the target either).
entries.press: Open the Corporation panel, find the rival's row (only shown once the corp is otherwise BL-068-discovered), click 'Declare Hostile', confirm 'Declare' in the popup ('Cancel' backs out).

args.name: counterparty
args.meaning: The corporation being declared hostile. May not be yourself.

preconditions: counterparty names a real, distinct corporation (rejected_invalid otherwise).
Not already hostile toward counterparty (rejected_state otherwise).
entries.expected_output: A directed row is inserted into world.corp_hostile_pairs (corp -> counterparty only; the reverse direction is unaffected — hostility is unilateral by design, an ambush the target does not have to agree to). Any existing friendship row between the two is dissolved atomically, and any pending friendship offer in either direction is withdrawn. A rejected declaration mutates nothing.
entries.reason_to_select: The predicate everything military-adjacent waits on (BL-315). Declaring hostile does not itself trigger any engagement — it only makes one legal later — but it also dissolves friendship on contact, so it is the one press that can undo a standing relationship as a side effect.

entries.surface: Corporation panel, Stance column.
entries.press: Open the Corporation panel, find the rival's row, click 'Offer Friendship'. Shows 'Offer sent' afterward until the target accepts, declines, or either party moves to hostile.

args.name: counterparty
args.meaning: The corporation being offered friendship. May not be yourself.

preconditions: counterparty names a real, distinct corporation (rejected_invalid otherwise).
Not already friends with counterparty (rejected_state otherwise).
Not currently hostile toward counterparty — return_to_neutral first (rejected_state otherwise).
No offer already pending in this direction (rejected_state otherwise; not a re-send).
entries.expected_output: A pending offer (corp -> counterparty) is inserted into world.corp_friend_offers. Friendship is NOT yet in effect — offer_friendship alone changes nothing about is_hostile/are_friends until the target calls accept_friendship. A rejected offer mutates nothing.
entries.reason_to_select: Friendship is deliberately the one stance that cannot be imposed — it requires both a genuine offer and a genuine accept, so a friendly row is always evidence both corps chose it, unlike hostility which is unilateral.

entries.surface: Corporation panel, Stance column. Shown only on a rival row carrying a pending offer FROM that rival TO the player.
entries.press: Open the Corporation panel; a row with an incoming offer shows 'Accept Friendship' instead of 'Offer Friendship'. Click it.

args.name: counterparty
args.meaning: The corporation whose offer is being accepted (the offerer). The acting corp is cmd.corp, the acceptor.

preconditions: counterparty names a real, distinct corporation (rejected_invalid otherwise).
A pending offer exists in the direction counterparty -> corp (rejected_state otherwise — there is nothing to accept).
entries.expected_output: The pending offer (counterparty -> corp) is erased, and a symmetric row is inserted into world.corp_friend_pairs under the canonicalised (min id, max id) key — both parties now read are_friends() true toward each other. A rejected accept mutates nothing.
entries.reason_to_select: The only way friendship becomes real. An offer alone (offer_friendship) is not a stance change by itself; this verb is the second half of the two-party handshake the model requires.

entries.surface: Corporation panel, Stance column. Shown whenever the row is currently Hostile or Friend.
entries.press: Open the Corporation panel, find the rival's row, click 'Return to Neutral'.

args.name: counterparty
args.meaning: The corporation being returned to neutral standing. May not be yourself.

preconditions: counterparty names a real, distinct corporation (rejected_invalid otherwise).
At least one of: the corp's own directed hostility toward counterparty, a shared friendship row, or a pending offer in either direction currently exists (rejected_state otherwise — nothing to clear).
entries.expected_output: Unilateral and asymmetric on hostility: clears ONLY the acting corp's own directed hostility toward counterparty (the reverse direction, if counterparty is separately hostile toward the corp, is untouched — that is counterparty's own row to release). Clears the shared friendship row if one exists (either party may dissolve a friendship) and any pending offer between the two in either direction. A rejected call mutates nothing.
entries.reason_to_select: The universal de-escalation press — the only one of the four verbs usable from every non-neutral state, and the one that lets a corp exit hostility unilaterally even though it could not enter friendship unilaterally.

entries.surface: Navigation rail slot 12, "Strategy readout"
entries.press: Click nav rail slot 12 to open the Strategy readout; click it again to close
preconditions: In game (not the menu or the generation screen)
entries.expected_output: The Strategy readout opens in the shell fold-out column, closing whatever ledger was open (the column holds one occupant). It aggregates each corporation's strategic decisions over a rolling 64-quarter window: with no corp selected, one must-have/should-have/nice-to-have bucket-split bar per corporation; with a corp selected, its bucket split quarter by quarter (a stacked band), its verb mix, and its reason tally. Score and margin figures are deliberately absent (candidates sort by priority bucket before score, so raw margins do not aggregate honestly). Clicking the slot while the readout is already open closes it (standing toggle rule).
entries.reason_to_select: To see WHAT STRATEGY IS EMERGING rather than the individual moves - the decision feed lists the moves; this shows the shape of a run. A corp living in must-have is defending its solvency; one living in nice-to-have is expanding unopposed.

entries.surface: Strategy readout, corporation selector
entries.press: Select a corporation from the readout's corp selector, or "All"

args.name: corp
args.meaning: "all" shows the per-corp bucket-split comparison; a corporation shows its full profile (bucket band by quarter, verb mix, reason tally)

preconditions: Strategy readout is open
entries.expected_output: The view switches between the all-corporations comparison and one corporation's full profile. The selection persists across selection changes elsewhere in the game - clicking a tile does not clear it.
entries.reason_to_select: The comparison answers 'who is winning the run and how'; the single-corp profile answers 'what is this corp's strategy made of'. Two different questions over the same window.
